articles.title: Ed Oliver faces painful family loss and receives support from the Buffalo Bills
articles.standfirst: The player is going through one of the most difficult moments of his life.
articles.summary: The player is going through one of the most difficult moments of his life.
articles.body:
Over the past few days, a rumor surrounding Ed Oliver’s personal life began gaining attention among Buffalo Bills fans , who were trying to understand what was happening with the player. What was initially surrounded by uncertainty and speculation ultimately had a much more painful explanation: the defensive tackle lost his two-year-old son .

The tragedy happened during the summer

The child died on June 28 in Houston , Texas, while Oliver was at home during the NFL offseason.

According to available reports, the boy drowned in a swimming pool after being found and taken to a hospital, where he was later pronounced dead.

The case remained under investigation by county authorities. In the weeks that followed, the family kept the tragedy away from the public eye, which is why the news was not immediately officially connected to the player .

Questions grew as Oliver continued working

The player reported to the team’s training camp in late July at St. John Fisher University in Rochester, New York , and took part in the team’s activities as usual.

There were no public signs that he was dealing with a tragedy of such magnitude. To those following Buffalo’s preparations from the outside, Oliver simply appeared focused on doing his job and getting ready for a season in which the Bills hope to compete for important goals once again .

But behind that routine was a completely different reality.

The Buffalo Bills finally confirmed the loss

As the news began spreading among fans, the Buffalo Bills made their support for Oliver public .

The team’s president of football operations, Brandon Beane , shared a message on behalf of the entire organization to stand with the player and his family as they grieve.

The statement described the loss as an unimaginable tragedy for any parent and made it clear that the team will continue supporting Oliver during this difficult time.

articles.title: The $2.2 billion stadium nightmare: The drama of the stands now shifts to the turf of the new Highmark Stadium
articles.standfirst: After complaints about obstructed views, the Bills are now dealing with problems on their brand-new playing surface
articles.summary: After complaints about obstructed views, the Bills are now dealing with problems on their brand-new playing surface
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills’ new $2.2 billion home was supposed to usher in a new era for the franchise. Instead, the early attention surrounding Highmark Stadium has shifted from problems in the stands to an unexpected issue on the field.

The Bills are tearing out and replacing the natural grass surface after preseason action exposed several concerns with the Kentucky bluegrass.

Bare patches, chunks of loose turf and damaged sections appeared across the field, with pieces of grass reportedly coming loose when players were tackled.

Technically, the field passed the NFL’s safety and playability standards. However, that wasn't enough to convince the Bills to leave things alone.

With three consecutive home games scheduled in Weeks 2 through 4, the organization decided it had an opportunity to address the surface before the regular season reaches its early home stretch.

Bills president of business operations Pete Guelli said the team wants to provide its players with the best possible playing conditions.

“We’re committed to having the best possible playing surface for our players,” Guelli said in a statement. “With a stretch of three consecutive home games early in the season, we decided it was the appropriate time to re-sod our field.”

A new surface for a new beginning

Questions about the field have also gained additional significance because quarterback Josh Allen has been very clear about his preference for natural grass.

During a recent discussion about playing surfaces, Allen said he believes grass is healthier for players and explained that he can physically feel the difference after practicing on artificial turf.

The Bills quarterback went further, describing painful burns he has suffered while playing on artificial surfaces.

"I've gotten numerous, numerous burns on my legs from artificial turf to the point where I can't sleep at night because it's bubbling over," said Allen. "It's very painful."

That makes Buffalo's decision to install natural grass at its new stadium particularly welcome news for its franchise quarterback. However, the surface has already encountered problems before the regular season has properly begun.

Guelli has defended the field, pointing out that it's a brand-new surface and suggesting that its foundation needs time to develop.

Still, the decision to replace the sod so soon demonstrates that the Bills aren't prepared to accept anything less than an excellent playing field.

The turf concerns come at an awkward time for the stadium. Fans had already criticized Highmark Stadium after getting their first major look at the venue during an August 8 open practice.

Images of seats with obstructed views spread across social media, with some supporters questioning whether they had been properly informed about what they'd see from their tickets.

Now, the focus has moved from the seats to the surface beneath the players.

If the new field performs as intended once the regular season begins, the preseason problems could quickly become a footnote. If issues return, however, the stadium's expensive debut could become an even bigger source of frustration for players and fans alike.

articles.title: Josh Allen follows wife Hailee Steinfeld into entertainment, launches 'Out of Pocket Studios'
articles.standfirst: The Buffalo Bills quarterback is expanding his off-field ambitions with a new production company while preparing for his ninth NFL season
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills quarterback is expanding his off-field ambitions with a new production company while preparing for his ninth NFL season
articles.body:
Josh Allen is adding another role to his already growing résumé.

The Buffalo Bills quarterback has officially launched Out of Pocket Studios, a new production venture that will allow the reigning NFL star to develop projects across entertainment, advertising and live experiences.

Allen will serve as the company's CEO and executive producer on its projects, giving him a direct role in shaping the content rather than simply lending his name to the business.

The move continues Allen's growing relationship with Skydance Sports, which signed him to an overall deal in 2025.

That agreement gave the quarterback an opportunity to develop scripted, unscripted and branded content, providing the foundation for what has now become Out of Pocket Studios.

For Allen , the new company represents an attempt to turn ideas away from the football field into tangible entertainment projects.

“Skydance Sports has given me a platform to turn the ideas I care most about into something real,” said Allen in a statement. “We’re excited to share what Out of Pocket Studios has created so far, and for everyone to see what we’re building from here.”

Lindsey Cohen has been appointed president of strategy and operations and will oversee the studio's day-to-day business.

The partnership gives Allen access to the infrastructure and entertainment expertise of Skydance while allowing him to develop his own creative identity. It is also an intriguing next step considering who Allen shares his life with.

His wife, Hailee Steinfeld , has been working in entertainment since she was a teenager and has built a career spanning film, television and music.

Steinfeld earned an Academy Award nomination for her performance in True Grit and has since appeared in projects including The Edge of Seventeen, Bumblebee, the Pitch Perfect franchise and the animated Spider-Verse films.

Allen , meanwhile, remains squarely in the middle of his football career. The 2026 season will be his ninth with Buffalo, where he has developed from a raw first-round quarterback into one of the NFL's most prominent players.

Allen's entertainment ambitions are already producing projects

The most notable aspect of Out of Pocket Studios is that Allen is not simply announcing a company with projects still years away.

Its initial slate is already taking shape.

The studio is behind America's Tailgate, a Labor Day television special for CBS, while NFL Play Action is scheduled to premiere Sept. 9. The latter will be hosted by Kyle Brandt and Ally Love , giving Allen's company an immediate presence in NFL-related programming.

Allen has also already sold a comedy series that he created, although additional information about the project, including its release date, has not yet been announced.

That early activity suggests Allen's ambitions extend beyond creating a production company as a future post-football project. He is beginning to build an entertainment portfolio while he is still playing at the highest level.

The timing makes sense. Professional athletes increasingly have opportunities to develop businesses and creative projects around their personal brands, but Allen's partnership with Skydance gives him access to an established Hollywood operation rather than requiring him to build everything independently.

Skydance Sports has already worked on a wide variety of sports-related productions, including documentaries, scripted entertainment and behind-the-scenes NFL projects.

Its portfolio includes NFL Draft: The Pick Is In, which takes viewers inside NFL draft rooms, and America's Team: The Gambler and His Cowboys, a documentary series about the Dallas Cowboys dynasty of the 1990s.

Allen's own popularity could also give the studio a valuable starting point. The quarterback won the NFL MVP award for the 2024 season and has established himself as one of the league's biggest stars, while Buffalo has reached the playoffs in all but one of his NFL seasons.

His immediate priority, however, remains football. The Bills will enter another season expecting Allen to lead their pursuit of a Super Bowl, meaning his responsibilities with Out of Pocket Studios will have to fit around the demanding schedule of an NFL quarterback.

For now, Allen is showing that his ambitions are not limited to what happens between the white lines.

If his playing career eventually takes him away from the NFL, Out of Pocket Studios could give him a ready-made second act in entertainment. But with projects already in production and more reportedly in development, Allen is making that transition long before his football career is finished.
